definition: Renown means widespread fame combined with a good reputation.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word renown. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know renown should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The marine biologist's renown grew with every reef her team brought back from the brink.
Recognition means people know your name; renown means your name travels widely and carries an excellent reputation with it.
Immortality goes past renown — fame so lasting that the name outlives its owner by centuries.

Fame is simply the state of being widely known — for anything at all, good, bad, or trivial. Renown is fame of a particular kind: the name travels far and carries an excellent reputation with it. A scandal can bring fame overnight; renown has to be earned.

Prominence means being important and noticeable — standing out where everyone can see you, a name always in the headlines. Renown does not need the spotlight: it is measured by how far and how favorably a name travels, and it can build quietly for decades.

The community orchestra in Dover Falls rehearsed in a church basement for thirty years.
Then a recording of their winter concert spread among conductors, and invitations began arriving — first from the state capital, then from festivals abroad.
By the time the players packed for their first international tour, the little orchestra's renown had outgrown the town on its own bus-stop sign.
The invitations spreading from the capital to festivals abroad show the orchestra's name traveling far beyond its home with an excellent reputation attached — that widespread, earned fame is renown.

renown: Immortality goes past renown — fame so lasting that the name outlives its owner by centuries.
The valley town of Cremora has no billboard and no airport, and its one hotel closes in winter.
Yet concert violinists on three continents can pronounce its name, because for two hundred years its workshops have turned out instruments of unusual warmth.
The town's renown rests on that sound alone.
No maker there advertises; a violin simply leaves the valley, gets played somewhere far away, and is admired, and its label is read aloud.
Ask a soloist in Seoul or Lisbon about Cremora and you will hear the same two things: they know the name, and they trust it.
